Surah al-Shura (Surat ash-Shura) [Meccan, except verses 23, 24, 25 and 26, which are Medinan; it has 53 verses; it was revealed after Fussilat]

﴿ʿAyn Sin Qaf﴾ God knows best what He means by it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 42, verse 3:

﴿Thus﴾ i.e., like that revelation ﴿He reveals to you﴾ revealed ﴿and to those before you﴾ ﴿Allah﴾, the doer of the revealing, ﴿the Mighty﴾ in His dominion ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 4:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, in dominion, creation and servitude. ﴿And He is the Most High﴾ above His creation, ﴿the Most Great﴾, the Grand.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 5:

"The heavens almost split apart" (read with ta' and ya') from above them" (read with nun, and in another reading with ta' and tashdid): that is, each one splits above the one next to it, from the greatness of Allah, the Exalted.

﴿And the angels glorify their Lord with His praise﴾: that is, while engaged in praise.

﴿And they seek forgiveness for those on the earth﴾: of the believers.

﴿Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving﴾ toward His friends ﴿the Merciful﴾ toward them.

Those who take protectors other than Him, [meaning the idols], Allah is Watchful over them [ḥafīẓ: Counting their deeds] so that He may recompense them. And you are not a guardian over them [and you have not been made responsible for them]. [The purpose is achieved from them; your duty is only to deliver the message.]

Thus (We have revealed to you) like that revelation, "We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn" (tukhawwif, i.e., frighten) "the Mother of Cities (Umm al-Qura) and those around it" (ay, the people of Makkah and all other people), "and warn" the people "of the Day of Gathering" (yawm al-jam', the Day of Resurrection, on which the creatures will be gathered), "there is no doubt" (rayb, i.e., shakk, "doubt") "about it. A party" of them "will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze" (al-sa'ir, i.e., the Fire).

If God had willed, He would have made them one community, i.e., upon one religion, which is Islam. ﴿But He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and the wrongdoers﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿have no protector nor helper﴾ who would avert the punishment from them.

﴿Or have they taken protectors besides Him?﴾ That is, the idols. Or it is disjunctive (munqati'a), meaning "rather" (bal), which is used for transition (al-intiqal), and the hamza is for denial (al-inkar), meaning: those who take protectors are not [in the right]. ﴿So God, He is the Protector﴾, that is, the Helper of the believers. The fa' (fa) is merely for coordination (li-mujarrad al-'atf).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 10:

﴿And whatever you differ about﴾ with the disbelievers ﴿concerning anything﴾ of the religion or other than it, ﴿its judgment﴾ is deferred ﴿to God﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, who will decide between you. Say, [to them]: ﴿That is God, my Lord; in Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn back﴾ in repentance, I return.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 11:

﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ (mubdi'uhuma, the one who brought them into being without precedent) ﴿He made for you from yourselves mates﴾ (ḥaythu khalaqa Ḥawwa' min ḍil' Ādam, in that He created Ḥawwa' (Eve) from a rib of Ādam) ﴿and of the cattle, mates﴾ (dhukūran wa-ināthan, males and females) ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾ (yadh'uukum, with the letter dhāl pointed, meaning yakhluqukum, He creates you) ﴿in it﴾ (fī, in the aforementioned arrangement of pairing; i.e., He increases you through it by means of procreation; the pronoun refers to humans and cattle by way of taghlīb, the dominance of one term over another) ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ (the kāf is extra, because He, exalted is He, has no like) ﴿and He is the All-Hearing﴾ (of what is said) ﴿the All-Seeing﴾ (of what is done).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 12:

﴿To Him belong the keys (maqaalid) of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., the keys to their treasuries of rain, plants and other things. ﴿He extends provision﴾, i.e., He widens it ﴿for whom He wills﴾, as a test; ﴿and restricts it﴾, i.e., He constricts it for whom He wills, as a trial.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 13:

﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, meaning he is the first of the prophets of the sharia (law), ﴿and that which We revealed to you and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you should establish the religion and not be divided therein﴾. This is the ordained law, enjoined and revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness). ﴿Hard is it for the polytheists what you call them to﴾, meaning it is great (kabura: became grievous or immense) upon them, namely tawhid. ﴿God chooses for it whom He wills﴾, that is, for tawhid, ﴿and guides to it whoever turns (yunib: returns in submission) to Him﴾, meaning whoever turns to His obedience.

Surah 42, verse 14:

﴿And they did not become divided﴾ i.e., the people of the religions became divided in the religion, some monotheists and some disbelievers, ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ of the Oneness (tawhid), ﴿out of rivalry﴾ from the disbelievers ﴿among themselves. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ regarding delaying the recompense ﴿until a specified term﴾ the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ by punishing the disbelievers in this world. ﴿And indeed those who were given the Scripture after them﴾ and they are the Jews and the Christians ﴿are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾ concerning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿doubt that causes suspicion﴾ (murib), i.e., one that brings about uncertainty.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 15:

﴿So for that reason﴾ (i.e., to the tawhid), ﴿call﴾ (O Muhammad) mankind ﴿and remain steadfast﴾ upon it ﴿as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires﴾ in abandoning it, ﴿and say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Book, and I have been commanded to act justly﴾ (ay, to be just) ﴿between you﴾ in judgment. ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds﴾, so each will be recompensed for his deed. ﴿There is no argument﴾ (khusumah, dispute) ﴿between us and you﴾, this being before he was commanded to wage jihad. ﴿Allah will gather us together﴾ on the Day of Return, for the decision of judgment, ﴿and to Him is the final destination﴾, the place of return.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 16:

﴿And those who dispute concerning﴾ the religion of ﴿Allah﴾, His Prophet, ﴿after it has been responded to﴾ by [people] accepting it through faith, because of the manifestness of His miracle, and they are the Jews, ﴿their argument is baseless﴾, false.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 17:

﴿Allah is the One who sent down the Book﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿with the truth﴾ — this is connected to "sent down." ﴿And the balance﴾ — the justice. ﴿And what will make you know﴾ — will inform you — ﴿that perhaps the Hour﴾ — i.e., its coming — "perhaps" (laʿalla) here suspends the verb "know" (yudrika) from taking effect on its object, and what follows it fills the place of the two objects.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 18:

﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾ They say: "When will it come?", thinking that it will not come. ﴿But those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾ fearful ﴿of it, and they know that it is the truth. Indeed, those who dispute﴾ argue ﴿concerning the Hour are in far error.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 19:

﴿Allah is Gentle (Latif) with His servants﴾: [He is gentle] with the righteous among them and the wicked, in that He does not destroy them with hunger because of their sins. ﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾: [He provides] each of them with what He wills. ﴿And He is the Strong﴾ over what He wills, ﴿the Mighty﴾, the One who prevails over His command.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 20:

﴿Whoever desires﴾ by his deed ﴿the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, i.e., its gain, which is the reward, ﴿We will increase him in his tilth﴾ by multiplication, so that a good deed is multiplied to ten and more. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it﴾ without multiplication, what has been apportioned for him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 21:

﴿Am﴾ (rather, or): ﴿Do they have﴾ for the disbelievers of Makkah ﴿partners﴾, namely their devils, ﴿who have prescribed for them﴾, i.e., the partners prescribed for the disbelievers ﴿of the religion﴾ (ad-din, the way of life) that is corrupt, ﴿that for which Allah has not given permission﴾, such as polytheism and the denial of resurrection. ﴿And were it not for the decree of separation﴾, i.e., the previous decree that the recompense is on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been judged between them﴾ and between the believers, by punishing them in this world. ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾, a painful one.

You see the wrongdoers, on the Day of Resurrection, fearful (mushfiqin, khA'ifin) of what they earned (of evil deeds in the world), lest they be recompensed for it, ﴿and it [i.e., the recompense for it] will befall them﴾ ﴿without doubt﴾ on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the meadows of the gardens﴾, the most delightful of them in comparison with those below them.

﴿That is what﴾ [Allah] ﴿gives good news of﴾ (from al-bishara, read both with a light and with a heavy form of the verb) ﴿to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say: I do not ask you for it﴾, that is, for conveying the message, ﴿any reward except affection among relatives.﴾ This is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception whose excluded item is not of the same category as what precedes it), meaning: "But I ask you to show affection to my relatives, who are also your relatives, for he [the Prophet] has kin in every clan of Quraysh." ﴿﴾ "And whoever earns" ﴿does, acquires﴾ "a good deed" ﴿an act of obedience﴾ "We increase for him therein good" ﴿by multiplying it﴾. "Indeed Allah is Forgiving" ﴿of sins﴾ "Appreciative" ﴿of the little, so He multiplies it﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 24:

﴿Am﴾ (rather/or), [they say, "He has invented against Allah a lie."] — by attributing the Qur'an to Allah the Exalted. ﴿If Allah wills, He would seal﴾ — bind — ﴿upon your heart﴾ — with patience over their harm by this statement and others; and He has done so. ﴿And Allah will erase the falsehood﴾ — which they have spoken — ﴿and will establish the truth﴾ — confirm it — ﴿by His words﴾ — revealed to His Prophet. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ — of what is in the hearts.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn, commentary on Surah 42 (ash-Shura), verse 25:

﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ from among them, ﴿and pardons the evil deeds﴾ for those who repent of them, ﴿and He knows what you do﴾ with the letter ya' (ي, "they do") and the letter ta' (ت, "you do") read.
﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ He answers them in what they ask.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 27:

﴿If Allah were to expand provision for His servants﴾ all of them, ﴿they would surely rebel﴾ all of them, meaning they would transgress ﴿in the earth. But He sends down﴾ with the light reading (bi-l-takhfif, reciting the verb with a single consonant rather than the doubled form) and its opposite (of the doubled form) of provisions ﴿"in measure as He wills"﴾ ﴿so He extends it to some of His servants and not others, and from expansion arises transgression﴾

﴿And it is He who sends down the rain﴾ the rain, ﴿after they have despaired﴾ they had given up hope of its descent, ﴿and spreads His mercy﴾ He spreads out His rain. ﴿And He is the Protector﴾ the Benefactor of the believers, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾ the One praised by them.

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [creation], ﴿and what He has scattered and spread throughout them of living creatures﴾, which are what crawls upon the earth, of humans and others. ﴿And He is able to gather them﴾ [for the Gathering] ﴿when He wills﴾. In the pronoun in ﴿their gathering﴾ (جَمْعهمْ) there is taghlīb (giving precedence to the rational over the non-rational), i.e., the masculine plural pronoun is used because the rational beings are included.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 30:

﴿Whatever affliction befalls you﴾ is an address to the believers. ﴿Of misfortune﴾ means calamity and hardship. ﴿It is because of what your hands have earned﴾ means what you have committed of sins. He expressed it with "hands" because most actions are performed by them. ﴿And He pardons much﴾ of them, so He does not requite for it. He, exalted is He, is too generous to requite again in the Hereafter. As for those who are not sinners, what befalls them in this world is for raising their ranks in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 31:

﴿And you are not⟩ O polytheists ﴿able to escape⟩ Allah by fleeing ﴿in the earth⟩ so as to elude Him, ﴿and you have not, besides Allah⟩ i.e., other than Him ﴿any protector or helper⟩ to repel His punishment from you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 32:

﴿And among His signs are the ships⁠—﴾ the ships ﴿sailing on the sea like mountains﴾ like the mountains in their greatness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 33:

﴿If He wills, He stills the wind, and they [the ships] remain motionless on its surface.﴾ [They become] ﴿motionless﴾, fixed, not moving ﴿on its surface. Indeed in that are signs for every ever-patient, ever-grateful one.﴾ That is the believer, who is patient in hardship and grateful in ease.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 34:

﴿أوْ يُوبِقهُنَّ﴾ "Or He destroys them," عُطِفَ عَلى يُسْكِنِ (this is conjoined to *yuskin*, "He stills"), meaning: يُغْرِقهُنَّ بِعَصْفِ الرِّيح بِأَهْلِهِنَّ (He drowns them with the force of the wind, along with their people). ﴿بِما كَسَبُوا﴾ "for what they have earned," meaning: أيْ أهْلهنَّ مِن الذُّنُوب (that is, their people, because of their sins). ﴿ويَعْفُ عَنْ كَثِير﴾ "and pardons much," مِنها (of them), فَلا يُغْرِق أهْله (so He does not drown their people).

The word ﴿wa-yaʿlamu﴾ ("and He knows") is read with a *ḍamma* (raf', nominative) as a resumptive clause (*mustaʾnaf*), meaning a new sentence that is not grammatically dependent on what precedes it. It is read with a *fatḥa* (naṣb, accusative) as conjoined (*maʿṭūf*) to an implied causal clause, meaning: He drowns them so that He may take vengeance on them, and so that He may know ﴿those who dispute concerning Our signs, that they have no escape.﴾ "No escape" means no refuge (*maḥīṣ*, a place of flight) from the punishment.

The negated clause ﴿mā lahum min maḥīṣ﴾ takes the place of the two objects of ﴿yaʿlamu﴾ ("He knows"). The negation is suspended from operating on the verb (*muʿallaq ʿan al-ʿamal*), so the verb is not governing it in the usual way.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 36:

﴿So whatever you have been given﴾ is addressed to the believers and others, ﴿of a thing﴾ from the household goods of this world, ﴿it is the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾, which one enjoys therein and then it passes away, ﴿but what is with Allah﴾ of reward ﴿is better and more lasting for those who believe and upon their Lord they rely﴾, and it is conjoined to what precedes it.

﴿Those who avoid the major sins and the abominations﴾, which are the things that necessitate the hudud (prescribed punishments). This is the conjunction of a part upon a whole (ʿaṭf al-baʿḍ ʿalā al-kull, where "al-baʿḍ" means the part and "al-kull" means the whole). ﴿And when they are angered, they forgive﴾, they overlook (offenses).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 38:

﴿And those who have responded to their Lord﴾ they answered Him in what He called them to of monotheism (tawhid) and worship; ﴿and established the prayer﴾ they maintained it; ﴿and their affair﴾ that which presents itself to them ﴿is by consultation among themselves﴾ they consult about it and do not hasten; ﴿and from what We have provided them﴾ We have given them ﴿they spend﴾ in obedience to God. And [the one mentioned] is a category.

﴿And those who, when tyranny (al-baghy) afflicts them, they defend themselves﴾ — al-baghy means the oppression (al-zulm); ﴿they defend themselves﴾ — a category; that is, they take retribution against whoever wronged them, with the like of his wrong.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 40:

﴿And the recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it﴾ The second is called "an evil deed" because of its resemblance to the first in form. This is evident in cases of retaliation for wounds. Some of them said: if he says to him, "May Allah disgrace you," he answers him, "May Allah disgrace you." ﴿But whoever pardons﴾ his wrongdoer ﴿and makes reconciliation﴾ of affection between himself and the one he pardons ﴿his reward is with Allah﴾, meaning Allah will surely reward him ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who initiate wrongdoing, so punishment is due to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 41:

﴿And whoever defends himself after being wronged﴾, i.e., after the wrongdoer has wronged him, ﴿those—there is no path (sabil) against them﴾, meaning, no blame (mu'akhadha).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 42, verse 42:

﴿Indeed, the blame (al-sabil) is only upon those who wrong people and transgress in the earth without right.﴾ They act (yaʿmalūna) ﴿in the earth without right﴾ by sins (bil-maʿasi). ﴿Those will have a painful punishment﴾ — painful (muʾlim).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 43:

﴿And whoever is patient and forgives﴾ — he refrains from retaliating, and pardons, overlooks. ﴿Indeed, that﴾ — the patience and the overlooking — ﴿is of the steadfast matters﴾ — i.e., of the things resolved upon, meaning the things required by the Sharia.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 44:

﴿And whoever Allah sends astray, for him there is no protector after Him﴾, i.e., no one who can guide him after Allah has led him astray. ﴿And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: "Is there any way of return?"﴾ to the world ﴿any way?﴾, a path.

And you will see them presented before the Fire, humbled by disgrace, looking at it with a furtive glance. ("Presented before it": the Fire.) "Humbled" means fearful and abject. "A furtive glance" means a weak look, stealthy; "min" here is either for the beginning of the limit (ibtida'iyyah) or in the sense of "bi" (with).

And those who believed will say: "Indeed the losers are those who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection," by their being made to dwell eternally in the Fire and by their not reaching the maidens (ḥūr) prepared for them in Paradise, had they believed. The relative clause is the predicate of "inna."

"Unquestionably, the wrongdoers" — the disbelievers — "are in a lasting punishment." This is part of what Allah the Exalted says.

And they will have no protectors to help them against Allah, other than Him, to ward off His punishment from them. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no way (sabil), meaning no path to the truth in this world or to Paradise in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 47:

﴿Respond to your Lord﴾ answer Him with monotheism (tawhid) and worship, ﴿before there comes a Day﴾ which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿from which there is no turning back from Allah﴾ meaning, once it comes, no one can turn it back. ﴿You will have no refuge﴾ that you can take refuge in, ﴿on that Day, and you will have no denial﴾ denial of your sins.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 48:

﴿Then if they turn away﴾ from responding, ﴿We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾ to watch over their deeds, by making them conform to what is required of them. ﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾ — and this was before the command to fight (jihad).

﴿And when We let man taste mercy from Us﴾ — a blessing such as wealth and health — ﴿he rejoices in it. But if an evil befalls them﴾ — the pronoun refers to man in the generic sense — ﴿a misfortune﴾ — a calamity — ﴿because of what their hands have sent forth﴾ — that is, what they have done. He expressed it by "hands" because most actions are carried out by them — ﴿then indeed man is ungrateful﴾ for the blessing.
﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows [children] upon whom He wills﴾ of children.

Or He weds them, males and females, [i.e., He makes them males and females,] and He renders barren whom He wills, so that he begets not nor is begotten. Indeed He is All-Knowing of what He creates, All-Powerful over whatever He wills.

﴿It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation﴾ (that He reveals to him) ﴿revelation﴾ in a dream or by inspiration, ﴿or﴾ (except) ﴿from behind a veil﴾, by making him hear His speech without seeing Him, as happened to Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, ﴿or﴾ (except) that He ﴿sends a messenger﴾, an angel like Jibril (Gabriel), ﴿who reveals﴾ by the messenger revealing to the one to whom he is sent, meaning he speaks to him, ﴿by His permission﴾, meaning Allah's permission, ﴿what He wills﴾, meaning Allah wills. ﴿Indeed He is Most High﴾ above the attributes of created beings (al-muhdathin), ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 42, verse 52:

﴿And thus﴾ i.e., like Our revelation to other messengers before you, ﴿We have revealed to you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿a spirit﴾, which is the Qur'an, by which hearts come to life, ﴿from Our command﴾ which We reveal to you. ﴿You did not know﴾, before the revelation to you, ﴿what the Book was﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿nor what faith was﴾, i.e., its laws and its signs. The negation suspends the verb from taking effect, and what follows it takes the place of the two objects. ﴿But We made it﴾, i.e., the spirit or the Book, ﴿a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed you guide﴾, by calling people through the revelation revealed to you, ﴿to a path﴾, a way, ﴿straight﴾, the religion of Islam.

﴿The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in dominion, creation and servitude. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned﴾ they come back (to Him).
